edges.description: Mutant C58G MLP engages BAG3 and induces a heat-shock chaperone response in homozygous knock-in hearts.

Lower MLP at the Z-disc releases calcineurin-NFAT signalling. Shown where MLP was depleted secondarily (MYH7 hypercontractility plus W4R) in human iPSC cardiomyocytes, and as calcineurin pathway activation in homozygous C58G knock-in hearts (about 20% of normal MLP); heterozygous knock-in hearts, with about 50% of normal MLP, showed no hypertrophic phenotype.
MLP-null human stem-cell cardiomyocytes develop impaired calcium handling.
Without MLP, human stem-cell cardiomyocytes develop disorganized sarcomeric ultrastructure, and strained rat myocytes lacking nuclear MLP develop disarrayed sarcomeres.

MLP is also expressed in skeletal muscle. Its loss produces only mild skeletal muscle abnormalities in mice, consistent with the mild skeletal muscle disease described in CSRP3 HCM carriers. The intermediate steps are not known.
Calcineurin-NFAT activity drives the hypertrophic growth programme.
Raised intracellular calcium is required for the hypertrophic phenotype of MLP-null human cardiomyocytes.
The remodelled, thickened left ventricle is clinical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
The hypertrophy is septum-predominant.
Profibrotic signalling and mild interstitial fibrosis accompany remodeling in homozygous knock-in hearts.
Impaired calcium handling that drives the hypertrophic phenotype.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a germline CSRP3 variant. Heterozygous HCM alleles are mostly missense changes at conserved residues of the first LIM domain (for example p.Leu44Pro, p.Ser54Arg/Glu55Gly and p.Cys58Gly), which binds alpha-actinin, plus the LIM2 allele p.Cys150Tyr. Biallelic truncating alleles remove the protein. The zinc-coordinating cysteine substitution p.Cys58Gly prevents zinc binding and folding of the first LIM domain.

nodes.description: Nonsense allele (NM_003476.5:c.364C>T). Found homozygous in a Polish HCM patient, and cosegregating with HCM in a three-generation Chinese family (zygosity not stated in the cited abstract).

LIM2 missense allele found in 11 of 6,456 Spanish HCM index cases and absent from other cardiomyopathy and control groups. Heterozygotes develop late-onset, low-risk HCM with highly age-dependent penetrance; the single homozygote was more severely affected.

LIM1 zinc-finger cysteine substitution. Cosegregates with HCM in a large four-generation family with genome-wide linkage. Abolishes zinc coordination, destabilizes MLP and reduces binding to alpha-actinin and N-RAP; the knock-in mouse loses about half of myocardial MLP as a heterozygote. A 2018 ACMG meta-analysis rated it the only likely pathogenic CSRP3 variant among those then reported.
LIM1 missense allele reported in HCM; depleted by the proteasome in cultured cells.
Double LIM1 missense allele reported in HCM; depleted by the proteasome in cultured cells.

Mavacamten improves exercise capacity and outflow obstruction in symptomatic obstructive HCM. The pivotal trial was not stratified by genotype and reports no CSRP3 carriers. In patient iPSC cardiomyocytes in which MLP was depleted secondarily to a sarcomeric variant combined with W4R, mavacamten raised MLP levels and suppressed calcineurin-NFAT signalling; whether it helps primary CSRP3 disease, in which MLP loss is caused by the CSRP3 variant itself, is untested.

evidence.snippet: Treatment with mavacamten improved exercise capacity, LVOT obstruction, NYHA functional class, and health status in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

nodes.description: The classic MLP-null mouse. Hearts are soft at birth with disrupted cytoarchitecture, and the mice develop dilated cardiomyopathy with hypertrophy and heart failure. Human complete loss of CSRP3 (biallelic truncation) gives adult HCM instead.

evidence.reference_title: MLP-deficient mice exhibit a disruption of cardiac cytoarchitectural organization, dilated cardiomyopathy, and heart failure.
evidence.snippet: Ultrastructural analysis revealed dramatic disruption of cardiomyocyte cytoarchitecture.

nodes.description: The first knock-in of a clearly pathogenic CSRP3 HCM allele. Homozygotes develop cardiomyopathy with diastolic and systolic dysfunction, increased heart weight, fetal and hypertrophic gene programmes, calcineurin pathway activation, mild fibrosis and a proteotoxic response. Heterozygotes lose about half of myocardial MLP but have no overt phenotype at baseline, with aging to 12 months, or after pressure overload.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant Muscle LIM Protein C58G causes cardiomyopathy through protein depletion.
evidence.snippet: In conclusion, the newly generated mouse model provides insights into the underlying disease mechanisms of cardiomyopathy caused by mutations in the non-sarcomeric protein MLP.

nodes.description: Reduced MLP at the Z-disc stretch-sensing complex is followed by increased calcineurin-NFAT activity and hypertrophic gene expression in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, and homozygous C58G knock-in hearts induce calcineurin-responsive Rcan1.4. MLP also anchors calcineurin at the Z-disc, and a mouse study after myocardial infarction found the opposite direction (halving MLP blunted calcineurin-NFAT activation and the hearts dilated). The authors of the human study propose that MLP both restrains and facilitates Z-disc calcineurin, so the net direction may depend on the setting; the allelic dilated entry (Dilated Cardiomyopathy 1M) models the reduced direction. See the discussion on this node.

nodes.description: Unstable mutant MLP is degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome system. In C58G knock-in mice, myocardial MLP falls to about 50% of normal in heterozygotes and about 20% in homozygotes, and two further HCM alleles are depleted in cultured cells. A C58G patient myocardium also showed reduced MLP, although MLP levels vary widely in failing and non-failing hearts. Biallelic truncating alleles give complete loss. Reduced functional MLP is therefore the common molecular end-point of the known pathogenic alleles; this has been shown in mice and cells, with one human tissue observation.

nodes.description: CRISPR/Cas9 CSRP3-null human embryonic stem cell line (H9) differentiated to cardiomyocytes. The cells develop hypertrophic features early and heart-failure features by 30 days, with impaired calcium handling; verapamil prevents the phenotype. Models complete loss of MLP, comparable to biallelic truncation.

Cardiomyocyte hypertrophy with a fetal and hypertrophic gene programme produces the asymmetric, septum-predominant left ventricular wall thickening of clinical disease. In the C58G knock-in mouse, homozygotes develop increased heart weight with diastolic and systolic dysfunction and mild fibrosis, while heterozygotes show at most a small rise in anterior wall thickness. In patients, wall thickening is typically moderate (mean maximal wall thickness 18 mm in p.Cys150Tyr carriers).

nodes.description: Knock-in of the common W4R allele. Heterozygous and homozygous mice develop age- and dose-dependent hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and heart failure with reduced MLP and weaker telethonin binding. Human carriers of W4R alone are usually unaffected, so the model overstates the allele's effect in humans.

evidence.reference_title: A common MLP (muscle LIM protein) variant is associated with cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: We now report the generation and detailed analysis of the corresponding Mlp(W4R/+) and Mlp(W4R/W4R) knock-in animals, which develop an age- and gene dosage-dependent hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and heart failure phenotype, characterized by almost complete loss of contractile reserve under catecholamine induced stress.

nodes.description: Profibrotic transcripts and mild interstitial fibrosis in homozygous C58G knock-in hearts. Heterozygous knock-in hearts show no fibrosis, and no CSRP3-specific human late gadolinium enhancement or histology series was found, so myocardial fibrosis is not curated as a patient phenotype.

nodes.description: Cardiomyocytes and engineered heart tissue from an HCM proband carrying MYH7 p.Arg723Cys and MLP W4R, with gene-edited corrections. Increased force destabilizes the Z-disc MLP complex, MLP falls and calcineurin-NFAT is disinhibited; correcting either variant, or mavacamten, rescues the phenotype. Here MLP depletion is secondary to a sarcomeric variant, so the model informs the downstream steps of CMH12 rather than its initiating lesion.

nodes.description: Standard HCM pharmacotherapy (beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, disopyramide) for symptoms and outflow obstruction. No CSRP3-specific clinical study exists. In MLP-null human stem-cell cardiomyocytes, verapamil restored calcium homeostasis and prevented the hypertrophic phenotype, a preclinical observation that fits the calcium node but has not been tested in patients.

In homozygous C58G knock-in hearts, the mutant protein binds the co-chaperone BAG3, heat shock proteins are induced, and a ubiquitin-proteasome reporter accumulates, indicating proteasomal overload. Whether this response contributes to hypertrophy, and whether it occurs at the lower mutant dose of heterozygous patients, is not known; the node has no downstream edge for that reason.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, MLP C58G interacts with Bag3 and results in a proteotoxic response in the homozygous knock-in mice, as shown by induction of Bag3 and associated heat shock proteins.

nodes.description: MLP forms a ternary complex with alpha-actinin, the main Z-disc actin cross-linker, and with N-RAP through separate binding sites. HCM missense alleles weaken both interactions. The authors of the C58G binding study proposed that the altered balance of this complex, and a compensatory rise in N-RAP when MLP falls, could lead to myocyte disarray. That step is a proposal and has not been tested.

evidence.snippet: We show that MLP can form a ternary complex with two of its previously documented myofibrillar ligand proteins, N-RAP and alpha-actinin, which indicates the presence of distinct, non-overlapping binding sites.

evidence.reference_title: Decreased interactions of mutant muscle LIM protein (MLP) with N-RAP and alpha-actinin and their implication for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Our data also show that, in comparison to wild-type MLP, the capacity of the mutated MLP protein to bind both N-RAP and alpha-actinin is significantly decreased.

nodes.description: Disorganized sarcomeric ultrastructure appears early in MLP-null human cardiomyocytes, and myocyte disarray is the characteristic histology of HCM. No CSRP3-specific human histology study was found, and no source states how cellular disarray feeds into tissue remodeling, so the node has no downstream edge.

evidence.reference_title: MLP-deficient human pluripotent stem cell derived cardiomyocytes develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and heart failure phenotypes due to abnormal calcium handling.
evidence.snippet: MLP-deficient hESC-CMs were found to develop phenotypic features of HCM early after differentiation, such as enlarged cell size, multinucleation, and disorganized sarcomeric ultrastructure.

nodes.description: Mild skeletal muscle disease was described in affected persons with CSRP3 missense variants in the 2008 linkage and segregation study. MLP is expressed in skeletal as well as cardiac muscle. The type and frequency of the skeletal findings are not given in the cited abstract, so no frequency is assigned.
